signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.89, holding just above its SMA20 at 156.79 while capped below the SMA50/200 cluster at 159.05/158.40. BoJ holds at 1.25%. COT positioning shows JPY leveraged funds net long +20,069 contracts in the 95th percentile with z at +1.57, reflecting heavy institutional backing after a massive WoW surge of +73,324. However, the options market flashes a sharp divergence: 25d risk reversals print at -1.88, demonstrating aggressive demand for JPY downside protection rather than topside participation. With VIX contained at 14.8, carry incentives dominate outright directional flows while the options market hedges against downside tail risk. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while spot holds above the SMA20. Catalyst: Next high-impact US data release. Risk: Daily close below 156.79 invalidating near-term momentum and accelerating options-led unwind.

signals.title: GBP/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: GBP/JPY trades at 210.01, driven by a pronounced weekly divergence across G10 peer performance. The G10 scorecard flags GBP as the top performer at +0.274% across 4 pairs while JPY is the clear laggard at -0.546% across 7 pairs, producing an 0.820% bilateral spread that triggers the thematic threshold. BoE policy at 3.75% against BoJ at 1.25% yields a +250bp nominal policy spread and a +275bp SONIA vs TONA carry advantage favoring sterling. In addition, the BEER valuation model flags the cross at z = -3.02 standard deviations cheap against model fair value of 215.47. The dovish reception to the BoJ tightening step allows the structural carry trade to reassert control. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/JPY, structural carry-driven trend continuation. Catalyst: Next high-impact UK data release. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% alongside sudden equity market volatility.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7126, situated below its SMA20 at 0.7168 but comfortably above the SMA50/200 cluster at 0.7087/0.7015. CFTC leveraged positioning shows AUD net long +59,299 contracts, placing positioning at the 97th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +2.11. While the RBA cash rate of 4.35% provides a 35bp policy premium 4.00% rate, the 2Y yield spread narrowed by 13bp over the last 5 sessions. ATM implied volatility sits at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.5%, generating a 1.0-point positive volatility risk premium that reflects hedging demand. With speculative positioning heavily crowded in the top decile, further topside progress faces positioning headwinds. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD, crowded speculative long limiting expansion. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold widely anticipated. Risk: Break below the 50-day SMA at 0.7087 triggering speculative liquidation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Technical Resistance + Macro Bias
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1480, pinned below its descending moving-average structure with the SMA20 at 1.1597, SMA50 at 1.1540, and SMA200 at 1.1633. The Fed at 4.00% maintains a 135bp policy rate advantage over the ECB at 2.65%, reinforced by a +141bp SOFR vs €STR carry premium. Leveraged positioning shows net short euro contracts at -51,355, sitting near the median at the 32nd percentile with z at -0.36. Real policy rates further underscore the policy divergence, with the US real rate restrictive at +1.59% compared to the Eurozone real rate of +0.30%. The technical downtrend remains reinforced by transatlantic policy rate differentials. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural policy spread favoring the dollar. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde Speech at 11:00 UTC. Risk: Daily close above the 50-day SMA at 1.1540 neutralizing immediate downward pressure.
